details.summary: A highly popular, short-acting CNS stimulant that works by blocking the reuptake of dopamine, serotonin, and norepinephrine. It is known to increase euphoria, confidence, sex-drive, focus, body temperature, and heart rate. Cocaine can cause severe vasoconstriction and is known to be cardiotoxic and have a high potential for compulsive redosing and addiction.
details.doseNote: Rapid onset. Depending on purity, dosage will vary

content.dose: Coffee ≈ 80–100 mg · energy drink ≈ 80 mg/250 ml · pills 100–200 mg.
content.prepare: Pure caffeine powder is dangerous: a teaspoon can kill. Never measure by eye.

spacing.label: Per day

content.dependence: Mild physical dependence: withdrawal headaches.

details.summary: Caffeine is a CNS stimulant and the most widely used psychoactive substance in the world. It is legal and unregulated in most parts of the world, and is found in many commonly sold products. It has a good safety profile, though regular heavy use can cause physical dependence and contribute to certain medical conditions.
details.doseNote: NOTE: The lethal dose for caffeine starts at approximately 3g. The average cup of coffee contains roughly 75-150mg of caffeine.

content.dose: Upper limit: 1.5 mg/kg for men, 1.3 mg/kg for women. Set your body below to calculate.
content.prepare: Test it (drug checking, Marquis + Simon's). Pills often contain 150 mg or more: start with a quarter or half.

spacing.label: 3-month rule
spacing.text: Serotonin needs time to recover. More often means weaker highs and harder comedowns.

content.dependence: Frequent use erodes the effects and mood.

risks.title: Overheating
risks.text: Take breaks from dancing, cool off and sip 300–500 ml of water per hour.

risks.title: Too much water
risks.text: Litres of water can cause fatal hyponatraemia. Sip, don't chug; isotonic drinks help.

risks.title: Redosing
risks.text: More MDMA brings more heat, strain and comedown, not more magic.

actions: Call 112 and say it's MDMA
Cool them: shade, wet cloths, fan
Don't force water; recovery position if unresponsive

details.summary: A short-acting dissociative anaesthetic and hallucinogen commonly used in medicine. It is the prototypical dissociative, and is widely used at sub-anesthetic doses recreationally. Small doses are comparable with alcohol, while larger doses are immobilising and lead to psychedelic experiences: the "K-Hole."
details.avoidText: Driving, walking, motor activity. Mixing with other depressants such as alcohol, benzodiazepines, and opioids.

details.summary: Alcohol is a CNS depressant that acts through the GABAₐ receptor, and is one of the most common strong psychoactives used by humans. It has a long history of use and its intoxicating effects are well-studied and documented. It remains legal in most parts of the world.
details.doseNote: NOTE: Alcohol consumption should be spread out over a few hours and ideally separated by water breaks. Check the label on alcohol for unit content

content.dose: Measure with an oral syringe. GBL is about twice as strong as GHB. Wait at least 2 hours before more.
content.prepare: Never with alcohol. Write down your dosing times or set a timer, and tell a friend.

spacing.label: Dependence
spacing.text: Daily use can cause dependence within weeks; withdrawal can be life-threatening: stop with medical help.

content.dependence: Rated moderate in 2007, but daily use leads to severe dependence.

risks.title: Tiny margin
risks.text: The step from euphoria to unconscious is very small.

risks.title: With alcohol
risks.text: Unconsciousness and stopped breathing.

risks.title: GBL burns
risks.text: Never drink it neat: dilute, and label the bottle.

actions: Recovery position, call 112
Stay with them: never let them 'sleep it off'
Tell paramedics how much and when

ghb/gbl.doseNote: Tends to induce heavy sedation roughly at 3g and higher.

details.summary: GHB and its prodrug GBL are GABA-B agonists with a very narrow dose-response curve. GBL converts rapidly into GHB in the body.
details.doseNote: NOTE: Tends to induce heavy sedation roughly at 3g and higher.

content.dose: Benzos differ 20× in strength: 0.5 mg alprazolam ≈ 10 mg diazepam.
content.prepare: Fake 'Xanax' and street pills often contain stronger benzos. Start with a fraction and don't redose.

spacing.label: Maximum course
spacing.text: Daily use beyond 2–4 weeks causes dependence. After regular use, never stop suddenly: taper.

content.dependence: Withdrawal after regular use can cause seizures.

risks.title: Breathing
risks.text: With alcohol, opioids or GHB, breathing can stop.

risks.title: Blackouts
risks.text: Memory loss and risky behaviour; you feel less high than you are.

risks.title: Withdrawal seizures
risks.text: After regular use. Taper with medical help.

signs: Very drowsy or can't be woken
actions: Recovery position, call 112
Stay with them
Tell paramedics about alcohol or opioids

details.summary: Benzodiazepines are GABA-A positive allosteric modulators used as anxiolytics, sedatives, and anticonvulsants (e.g. diazepam, alprazolam, clonazepam).

content.dose: Potency varies 100× between opioids (fentanyl and nitazenes work in micrograms) and tolerance drops after a few days off.
content.prepare: Carry naloxone, never use alone, test for fentanyl or nitazenes and try a small test dose first.

spacing.label: After any break
spacing.text: Tolerance drops within days. After detox, hospital, prison or a pause, use far less.

content.dependence: Physical dependence develops within weeks of daily use.

risks.title: Breathing stops
risks.text: The main cause of death, much worse with alcohol, benzos or GHB.

risks.title: Fentanyl & nitazenes
risks.text: Hidden in heroin and fake pills. Active in micrograms.

risks.title: Infections
risks.text: Never share needles or equipment: HIV, hepatitis C.

signs: Can't be woken; slow or no breathing, gurgling
actions: Call 112 and give naloxone; repeat after 2–3 min if needed
Rescue breaths or CPR; then recovery position
Stay: naloxone can wear off before the opioid

details.summary: Opioids act on mu-opioid receptors, producing analgesia, sedation, and respiratory depression. Includes heroin, morphine, oxycodone, fentanyl, and others.

content.dose: Ceiling effect: more tramadol mainly adds seizure risk, not more euphoria.
content.prepare: Avoid with epilepsy, antidepressants or other serotonergic drugs.
content.marginNote: No safety-ratio data. Seizure risk rises above ~300 mg; never exceed 400 mg/day.

spacing.label: Dependence
spacing.text: Daily use leads to opioid dependence and a difficult withdrawal.

content.dependence: Opioid dependence plus antidepressant-like withdrawal.

risks.title: Seizures
risks.text: Risk rises with dose and with stimulants.

risks.title: Serotonin syndrome
risks.text: With SSRIs, MDMA, MAOIs or DXM.

risks.title: Breathing
risks.text: With alcohol, benzos or other opioids.

actions: Call 112
Give naloxone if breathing is slow
Protect their head during a seizure, then recovery position

tramadol.doseNote: Tramadol has a ceiling dose where recreational effects are not increased. There is a risk of seizures at doses over 300mg or less for indivudals predisposed. Tramadol decreases the seizure threshold. Caution is strongly recommended. Dosing insufflated is ineffective.

details.summary: A synthetic opioid analgesic, tramadol is used to treat moderate pain and can be considered a medium-strength opioid. Tramadol has the unusual effect of being a serotonin releasing agent and a serotonin reuptake inhibitor. As a consequence, care should be taken to not ingest tramadol in excess due to the risk of serotonin syndrome. There is a risk of seizures at doses over 300mg or less for individuals predisposed.
details.doseNote: NOTE: Tramadol has a ceiling dose where recreational effects are not increased. There is a risk of seizures at doses over 300mg or less for indivudals predisposed. Tramadol decreases the seizure threshold. Caution is strongly recommended. Dosing insufflated is ineffective.

content.dose: Edibles: start with 5 mg THC or less and wait 2 hours. They last 4–10 hours.
content.prepare: Skip the tobacco; vaping flower is gentler on the lungs. Don't drive for at least 6 hours.
content.marginNote: No known fatal overdose. Greening out is unpleasant but passes.

spacing.label: Tolerance break
spacing.text: Daily use builds dependence. A 2–4 week break resets tolerance.

content.dependence: About 1 in 10 users become dependent, more with daily use.

risks.title: Anxiety & panic
risks.text: Common with high-THC strains and edibles.

risks.title: Psychosis
risks.text: Higher risk with high THC, daily use, youth or a family history.

risks.title: Synthetics
risks.text: Sprayed 'CBD weed' and vapes can contain synthetic cannabinoids: seizures.

actions: Sit or lie down somewhere calm
Sip water or a sugary drink; reassure
Call 112 for chest pain, seizures or unconsciousness

details.summary: A common and widely used psychoactive plant, which is beginning to gain legal status for medical and even recreational use in some parts of the world. Usually smoked or eaten, primary effects are relaxation and an affinity towards food - a state described as being 'stoned.'
